#2570. Mainz vs. FC Bayern preview: Can the hosts trouble the Bavarians again?

Bayern Munich will look to return to winning ways in the Bundesliga when they travel to Mainz 05 on Saturday, with the league leaders facing a side desperate to end their recent slump.

The Bavarians head into the Matchday 9 encounter following a frustrating run of results, having drawn four of their last eight competitive fixtures. Their most recent Bundesliga draw came against Borussia Dortmund, when Bayern dominated proceedings but were denied victory by Fabio Silva's late equaliser in the 89th minute.

Despite their recent struggles to turn dominance into victories, Vincent Kompany's side remain favourites against a Mainz team that has lost four of its last five competitive matches. The hosts most recently suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat against newly promoted SV Elversberg.

Saturday's encounter kicks off at 15:30 CET at the MEWA Arena.

Bayern assistant coach Aaron Danks, who remains in charge during Vincent Kompany's absence, confirmed that Jamal Musiala and Aleksandar Pavlović have returned to team training.

However, Musiala will not be available against Mainz, while Pavlović's involvement depends on how he responds physically. Manuel Neuer has also returned to training and is expected to feature.

Luis Díaz and Serge Gnabry remain sidelined with hamstring injuries. Alphonso Davies could also be rested due to workload concerns, although a limited appearance remains an option.

Mainz, meanwhile, must cope without Stefan Posch and Phillipp Mwene, who are both suspended. Head coach Urs Fischer will therefore need to make defensive adjustments after his side conceded four goals against Elversberg.

1. Mainz have enjoyed recent success against Bayern

Mainz have won four of their last six home Bundesliga meetings with Bayern. Their most recent encounter in April ended in a 4-3 victory for the Bavarians after Mainz had established a three-goal lead.

The visitors are unbeaten in their last 30 Bundesliga away matches, recording 22 wins and eight draws. Interestingly, their last away defeat came against Mainz in December 2024.

Eight of Mainz's 17 league goals this season have originated from their right flank, a Bundesliga-best figure. Anthony Caci has been particularly influential with three goals and three assists. Mainz have also scored five goals through substitutes this season, compared to Bayern's two.

#2569. England’s Dutch coach Sarina Wiegman extends contract until 2029

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch football coach Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract with the England women’s team by two years, taking her up to the 2029 European Championships.

Wiegman, 56, led the team to two European titles in 2022 and 2025, as well as their first World Cup final in 2023, when they lost to Spain.

Prior to that she won the European Championships with the Dutch national team in 2017 and reached the World Cup final two years later, losing 2-0 to the United States.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” she said in a statement released by the English Football Association (FA).

“Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as “an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments”. He added: “There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments.”

Commentators had widely expected the Dutchwoman to leave her post after next year’s World Cup, after England failed to qualify automatically for the tournament.

A 4-0 loss to Spain in June, the team’s heaviest defeat since Wiegman took charge, means they will have to come through a play-off tournament with Greece, Ukraine and Slovakia to reach the finals in Brazil.

Wiegman said: “Anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come.

“We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.”

#2566. PSV hold on to book narrow Champions League win in Porto

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV survived a second-half onslaught in Porto to secure their first win of the Champions League group stages.

Guus Til scored the only goal when he tapped in from close range after Esmir Bajraktarevic’s shot had come back off the post and was steered across goal by Sven Mijnans.

The Eindhoven club were worth their narrow lead against Francesco Farioli’s side after dominating possession in the first half, but rarely troubled Diogo Costa in the Porto goal.

Til went close with a header early in the second half before putting PSV ahead in the 57th minute.

But the visitors had to defend heroically as Porto poured forward in search of an equaliser, aided by an increasingly fragile Matej Kovar.

The goalkeeper put his defenders in jeopardy with a weak clearance in the 72nd minute, but redeemed himself by saving Victor Froholdt’s shot with his chest before Lutsarel Geertruida blocked the follow-up from Pepê.

A minute later Kovar was left stranded after he rushed out of his penalty area, but Sergiño Dest managed to hack the ball away before Alberto Costa could poke it into the open goal.

At the other end, substitute Denis Man came close to scoring a second for PSV with his first touch when his curling shot beat Costa but failed to sneak inside the post.

The 1-0 win lifts PSV to a provisional 16th place in the Champions League table at the halfway stage of round three, while Porto are still looking for their first point.

Their next match is at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, who will make the short trip to Eindhoven on November 4.

#2563. RB Leipzig vs. Augsburg preview: Hosts aiming to maintain perfect home record

Leipzig are currently sitting in fourth place after winning five, drawing one and losing two of their eight Bundesliga games. Martín Demichelis’s side have claimed back-to-back league wins since losing 6-1 away to Bayern Munich last month. Die Roten Bullen cruised to a 4-0 home win over Elversberg before they claimed a 2-0 away victory against Schalke 04 last weekend.

Unfortunately for Leipzig, they were unable to take anything from their Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Manchester City, despite coming from behind on a couple of occasions at the Red Bull Arena. Ridle Baku struck in the early stages of the second period to cancel out a first-half own goal, before Antonio Nusa responded to Enzo Fernández’s effort. However, Leipzig could not find a response to Erling Haaland’s 78th-minute goal, as they fell to their third defeat of the Champions League campaign.

While they lost 3-2 in front of their supporters in midweek, Leipzig will head into Saturday’s fixture with the only perfect home record in the division. They are also the only team yet to concede a home league goal, having won their four Bundesliga home games by a combined 18-0 scoreline.

They will certainly fancy their chances of picking up another win on Saturday, considering they have won each of their previous seven meetings with Augsburg at the Red Bull Arena.

Leipzig remain without the services of Assan Ouédraogo and Marc Guiu, while Max Finkgräfe is a major doubt after missing the defeat to Man City. Nusa was forced off against Enzo Maresca’s side and will need to be assessed ahead of Saturday’s fixture.

Click here for Leipzig's predicted lineup.

Augsburg are in 10th position and two points above the bottom three after winning two, drawing three and losing three of their eight matches this season. The Fuggerstädter have gone six consecutive games without a win since starting the Bundesliga campaign with back-to-back victories.

Michael Gregoritsch scored the opener in last weekend’s clash against his former club Freiburg, but it ultimately counted for very little as Augsburg conceded twice in the second half as they fell to a 2-1 loss at WWK Arena.

After losing on home turf, Manuel Baum’s side will now head on their travels with the primary objective of avoiding a third consecutive away loss. The Fuggerstädter shipped seven goals across their last two away defeats against Werder Bremen and Elversberg, highlighting a key area for improvement if they are to take anything from Sunday’s contest.

Their hopes of a positive result will be tempered by the fact they have only taken one point from their previous 10 Bundesliga away meetings with RB Leipzig, which means they are still searching for their first top-flight victory at the Red Bull Arena.

Baum is unable to call upon the services of Juma Bah, Calvin Brackelmann, Noahkai Banks and Steve Mounié. Meanwhile, Tim Breithaupt is back in training and pushing to make a matchday squad for the first time this season.

#2562. Pancaro: “L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione”

Dall'avvio da record alla gestione della pressione: l'analisi di Giuseppe Pancaro sulla straordinaria partenza biancoceleste.

Giuseppe Pancaro, intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, ha analizzato il super momento della Lazio: la forza del gruppo, i successi senza pubblico e la gestione saggia degli obiettivi futuri.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Come sto vivendo questo momento Lazio? E' una Lazio bellissima, non è un momento. Ventotto punti in 10 gare non è un caso. C'è del valore, grande merito da parte di Gattuso. Finalmente anche la soddisfazione per i tifosi che da anni non sognavano più e adesso stanno gioendo.

Ancora più sorprendente fare questi risultati senza tifosi all'Olimpico? Questo è un ulteriore merito di questo gruppo perché la difficoltà ambientale è oggettiva da anni. La sensazione è che loro ora non avvertano questo problema. Sicuramente giocare una gara come quella col Cagliari davanti a 13000 spettatori rispetto ad uno stadio pieno qualcosa toglie sempre. Questa squadra è talmente forte, concentrata, unita e compatta che riesce ad andare oltre.

C'è un momento in ogni stagione in cui ci si accorge che l'obiettivo postosi è cambiato. Quale sarà questo momento in cui magari dai 40 punti si passa a pensare ad una coppa europea? Gattuso in tal senso è bravissimo. L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione. Eventualmente penso se ne possa parlare in primavera, al momento fanno benissimo a giocare pensando ad una gara alla volta senza mettersi addosso pressione.

#2560. Feyenoord second best to Betis as Isco is on the spot for CL win

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord endured a frustrating evening in Spain as a penalty by Real Betis’s outstanding player, Isco, secured a 1-0 win for the La Liga side.

The Rotterdammers were second best for most of the game, but held out until the 59th minute, when Abde Ezzalzouli’s cross hit the arm of Jeremiah St. Juste in front of goal.

Isco, who was at the heart of Betis’s attacks all evening, grabbed the ball and gave Tjark Ernst no chance from the penalty spot.

Ernst had made good saves from former AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and Marc Batra to keep Feyenoord in the game in the first half, but Feyenoord had the best chance of the opening period when Gjivai Zechiël shot over the bar from close range.

The visitors had a claim for a penalty of their own turned down in the 68th minute when Givairo Read claimed he had been pushed by Ezzalzouli, but referee Simone Sozza waved the appeals away.

The result leaves Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side in 26th place in the Champions League table, with Internazionale up next in De Kuip on November 3.

#2559. Lazio, Liverani frena sullo scudetto: Gattuso pensa gara per gara

L’ex centrocampista guarda alla trasferta di Napoli: una buona prestazione darebbe entusiasmo durante la sosta.

La Lazio è prima da sola, ma Fabio Liverani invita a non parlare ancora di scudetto. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, L’ex centrocampista biancoceleste considera la qualificazione in Champions League un grande risultato e condivide la scelta di Rino Gattuso di affrontare una partita alla volta. In collegamento con Radio Sei, durante la trasmissione Quelli che hanno portato il calcio a Roma, ha parlato anche della prossima sfida con il Napoli, della vittoria sul Cagliari e di Belahyane e Isaksen.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La trasferta di Napoli è, per Liverani, un’occasione per arrivare alla sosta con ulteriore entusiasmo. Conta il risultato, ma conta anche la prova della squadra: «Fare bene a Napoli sarebbe la ciliegina sulla torta. Un risultato positivo, ma soprattutto una prestazione positiva, permetterebbe di lavorare durante la sosta con grande entusiasmo». L’ex biancoceleste ricorda che la Lazio raggiungerà comunque la pausa da capolista, indipendentemente dall’esito della gara.

Sulle ambizioni stagionali, invece, il suo auspicio è preciso: «Auguro alla Lazio di arrivare in Champions League. Parlare di scudetto è difficile, ma anche la Champions, considerando quello che si diceva in estate, sarebbe un grande risultato». Liverani richiama la lunghezza del campionato e le insidie ancora da affrontare. Per questo approva l’approccio di Gattuso, concentrato su una gara alla volta: a suo giudizio, il tecnico ha costruito così il percorso della squadra.

Liverani torna poi sul successo contro il Cagliari, arrivato nella terza partita in sette giorni. La Lazio, osserva, non è stata brillante. Proprio per questo dà valore al risultato: «Vincere una gara del genere ha un significato importante, perché dimostra che questa squadra ha raggiunto una certa maturità».

Secondo l’ex centrocampista, la posizione in classifica porta anche una maggiore attenzione da parte delle avversarie, che proveranno a contenere i principali pericoli biancocelesti. Cita il Cagliari e la scelta di schierare Fadera. La vittoria, nella sua lettura, è stata diversa dalle altre: la Lazio è riuscita a portarla a casa pur incontrando difficoltà.

#2557. Bayern draw up four-man shortlist to find backup and competition for Díaz

Currently lacking a natural alternative to Luis Díaz on the left wing, Bayern Munich are reportedly considering a move for a young winger who could provide backup and competition for the Colombian international ahead of next summer.

According to Bild's Bayern Insider podcast, the German champions have four young wingers on their radar: Oskar Pietuszewski (FC Porto), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Antonio Nusa (RB Leipzig) and Wael Mohya (Borussia Mönchengladbach).

Pietuszewski, an 18-year-old Polish winger, is reportedly at the top of Bayern's shortlist after impressing the club's scouting department in recent months. The youngster, who only joined Porto from Polish side Jagiellonia Białystok in January, is understood to have a €60 million release clause in his contract.

As for Ngumoha, Bayern were already showing interest in the Liverpool youngster last summer and were reportedly prepared to offer €72 million for the 18-year-old. However, the Reds were unwilling to let him leave at the time. With Ngumoha under contract until 2028, the situation could potentially change next summer.

Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl is said to be a particularly big admirer of Antonio Nusa. However, a move for the 21-year-old RB Leipzig star would also be expensive, potentially costing even more than either of the two aforementioned youngsters.

Finally, 17-year-old Wael Mohya, who recently received his first senior Germany call-up, is also reportedly on Bayern's radar. The Bavarians have apparently been in contact with the youngster's representatives for some time.

With Díaz currently sidelined, Alphonso Davies has recently filled in on the left wing for Bayern, while Nathaniel Brown could be deployed there against Mainz this weekend if the Canada international is deemed in need of a rest.

#2554. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

Il settore ospiti del Maradona dovrebbe restare chiuso per Napoli-Lazio, in programma domenica 8 novembre alle 12:30. Secondo quanto riportato da Radio Laziale, la trasferta sarà vietata ai sostenitori biancocelesti. CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il provvedimento dovrebbe impedire ai residenti nella Regione Lazio di acquistare biglietti per la partita. La restrizione non riguarderebbe soltanto il settore ospiti, ma anche gli altri settori dello stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Per i tifosi la notizia arriva dopo settimane segnate da una forte partecipazione alle trasferte della squadra.

Nei giorni scorsi l’Osservatorio Nazionale sulle Manifestazioni Sportive (ONMS) aveva rinviato la valutazione della gara al Comitato di Analisi per la Sicurezza delle Manifestazioni Sportive (CASMS). L’Osservatorio aveva inoltre invitato a non avviare la vendita dei biglietti destinati ai sostenitori ospiti.

Se l’orientamento sarà confermato, la Lazio affronterà la trasferta senza i propri sostenitori provenienti dal territorio laziale. La limitazione all’acquisto dei biglietti, così come prospettata, si estenderebbe anche ai posti fuori dal settore ospiti.

Il possibile stop arriverebbe dopo una serie di partite lontano dall’Olimpico seguite da migliaia di sostenitori biancocelesti. A Reggio Emilia, in particolare, circa 10mila tifosi della Lazio hanno accompagnato la squadra, con una presenza significativa sugli spalti.

La partecipazione delle ultime settimane aveva alimentato le aspettative anche per la sfida al Maradona. Per i sostenitori, la partita con il Napoli rappresentava un appuntamento sentito sia per il valore della gara sia per la volontà di continuare a seguire la formazione biancoceleste in trasferta.

Il divieto interromperebbe questa sequenza di trasferte molto partecipate. Dopo l’esodo di Reggio Emilia, i tifosi residenti nel Lazio rischiano dunque di non poter assistere alla partita di Napoli, neppure acquistando un posto in un settore diverso da quello ospiti.

#2546. Top five football betting tips and tricks

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

If you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

#2544. Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”

A late bloomer, José Miguel da Rocha Fonte has become one of the Portugal’s best-known professional footballers, which is no mean feat considering he was playing in the lower leagues in England well past his mid-twenties. Sheer determination saw Fonte gradually climb his way to the top, making it to the English Premier League with Southampton for whom he made 288 appearances and became captain and cult hero.

Yet the best part of his journey was only beginning. José Fonte would go on to play a major role in Portugal’s Euro 2016 triumph, playing all the knockout matches, and this season captained Lille to a sensational Ligue 1 title, with the northerners overcoming PSG despite a huge shortfall in budget compared to the Parisians.

Diogo José Teixeira da Silva was born in 1996 and he is one of the youngest and yet very popular footballers from Portugal. His performances since signing for Liverpool earlier this season mark him down as one of the best emerging players in the world. Known for his non-stop energetic style of play, he accumulated 13 goals for the English giants, despite missing a sizeable chunk of the middle of the season with injury.

Signed by Atletico Madrid for a whopping 126 million euros two years ago, the silky-skilled forward has the talent to take over from Cristiano Ronaldo as the country’s new golden boy when the Portugal captain eventually hangs up his boots. Félix has yet to hit if full stride in the Spanish capital, but has still shone brightly on occasions. In November he won the Player of the Month award in La Liga. He may yet be Portugal’s main man at the Euros.

Football is by far the most watched and played sport in the world, which makes the achievements of a country with a population of just 10 million people even more extraordinary. You can even make an argument that Portugal has become known first and foremost as a country that produces many of the best footballers and coaches of today. #2533. Feyenoord facing fireworks fine after 3-0 loss to Internazionale

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”

#2529. Lazio, accordo Mizuno in scadenza: Napoli a 18 milioni più bonus

Il contratto tecnico biancoceleste si avvicina alla scadenza; quello del Como terminerà il 30 giugno 2027.

Il contratto della Lazio con Mizuno è in scadenza: per il club biancoceleste si aprirà la possibilità di chiedere una sponsorizzazione tecnica più generosa di quella attuale. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Il confronto passa anche dalle cifre del Napoli, che con Armani è arrivato a 18 milioni di euro più 2,5 di bonus.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L’intesa biancoceleste si avvicina alla conclusione in una fase in cui gli accordi tecnici dei club presentano valori molto diversi. Alla scadenza, la Lazio potrà puntare a condizioni economiche migliori rispetto a quelle previste dal contratto attuale.

Tra gli accordi richiamati nel confronto figurano anche quelli della Roma con Adidas e della Fiorentina con Joma. Le cifre dei due club offrono altri riferimenti accanto al contratto della Lazio.

Il Napoli ha rinnovato l’intesa con Armani dopo le prime stagioni da 9 milioni di euro più uno di bonus. Il nuovo accordo vale 18 milioni di parte fissa e altri 2,5 di bonus. Alla scadenza, prevista nel 2028 per l’intesa del 2023, è ritenuta probabile una revisione al rialzo, anche se resta da capire di quale entità. Aurelio De Laurentiis viene indicato come abile nell’ottenere condizioni favorevoli nei contratti commerciali.

Il quadro delle sponsorizzazioni entra in una nuova fase anche con l’accordo del Milan con Adidas: 500 milioni di euro in dieci anni a partire dal 2028. La Roma riceve invece 5 milioni più bonus dall’intesa con lo stesso marchio, una cifra giudicata bassa rispetto alle valutazioni degli altri club citati.

Per la Fiorentina, il contratto con Joma prevede complessivamente 20 milioni in cinque anni, pari a 4 milioni a stagione.

#2528. Opinion: The morality of football

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

#2527. PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

#2526. Lazio, Hernanes crede nella tenuta stagionale e avverte l’Inter

Per l’ex centrocampista, i biancocelesti giocano con intensità; i nerazzurri devono ritrovare energia e fare i conti con alcune assenze.

Hernanes ritiene che la Lazio possa mantenere il proprio rendimento per tutto il campionato. L’ex centrocampista brasiliano ne ha parlato a margine di un evento del Sigma World di Roma, commentando la prima parte di stagione biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews, Ha poi rivolto la sua attenzione all’Inter, che considera ancora la squadra più forte ma dalla quale si aspetta una reazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

«La Lazio ha il potenziale per poter durare tutto il campionato», ha dichiarato Hernanes, secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews. Per il «Profeta», la squadra può contare su un allenatore vincente, che conosce la strada per la gloria e le ha trasmesso la propria onestà calcistica: scendere in campo dando tutto.

È questo, a suo giudizio, ciò che emerge dal gioco dei biancocelesti. Hernanes descrive una formazione intensa, con i valori giusti in ogni posizione, e sottolinea la qualità dei giocatori. «È una bellissima squadra che sta rendendo al 100%», ha aggiunto.

Parlando dell’altra sua ex squadra, Hernanes ha ricordato che nel calcio nessuna vittoria è acquisita prima di giocare: bisogna scendere in campo e dare il massimo. Pur ritenendo l’Inter la più forte, vede nei nerazzurri gli effetti della vittoria dello scorso anno. «Stanno ancora giocando con la pancia piena dopo la vittoria dello scorso anno», ha osservato.

Secondo il brasiliano, il calo di energia può avvenire inconsciamente. Finora, a suo avviso, l’energia impiegata era sufficiente; ora però l’Inter comincia a complicarsi la vita. Per questo, ha concluso il suo richiamo, i nerazzurri «devono svegliarsi».

Antonio Nusa's involvement for RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga this Saturday against FC Augsburg remains up in the air.

The Norwegian has been struggling with muscular problems following a couple of intense weeks for the Saxony-based club.

Following the 3-2 loss to Manchester City in midweek in which he was subbed off, Martin Demichelis has hinted at giving Nusa a rest.

“We only trained on the pitch for 25 minutes. Warm-up and then a rondo, so no tackles or sprints,” Demichelis said at his press conference.

Xavi Hernandez has his first win as Netherlands head coach as a Mexx Meerdink double led Oranje to a 2-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League.

Xavi made two changes from the side that drew with Germany as Mexx Meerdink replaced the injured Brian Brobbey up front while Joey Veerman came in for Quinten Timber.

Netherlands dominated from the start but they were forced into an early change when Cody Gakpo suffered a knock and Ruben van Bommel came on.

After half an hour, Crysencio Summerville was clipped in the box and Meerdink made it 1-0 from the penalty spot. It was almost 2-0 before the break but Denzel Dumfries could not convert when through on goal.

Serbia made a double change at the break with Luka Jovic and Dusan Tadic coming on. A minute into the second half, the change worked as Jovic was given space in the box to net after Netherlands failed to clear the ball.

Netherlands went in search of the lead again but Tijjani Reijnders blazed a huge chance over while Ruben van Bommel hit the post. Meerdink did eventually make it 2-1 with a lovely finish after a quick 1-2 with substitute Guus Til.

There was to be no hattrick for Meerdink as he was brought off and Netherlands played the final ten minutes with Til through the middle.

Serbia pressed for a late equaliser but the Netherlands had a golden chance to make it 3-1 when Til found himself in on goal. He had Summerville and Van Bommel to his left but overhit the pass and the later’s finish was too weak to find the net.

The Netherlands held on for the victory which takes them to the top of the group with a clash against Greece next on Thursday.

FT Serbia 1-2 NetherlandsXavi’s first win as Meerdink scores a double. Could have been more if not for some poor finishing

An injury-hit Netherlands side battled back to draw 2-2 against Greece in the Nations League.

Xavi was forced into changes with Cody Gakpo and Jan Paul van Hecke dropping out of the squad. Tijjani Reijnders and Ryan Gravenberch also dropped to the bench with Quinten Timber, Guus Til, Jurrien Timber and Ruben van Bommel starting.

Greece have been in good form recently and their confidence was clear from the start. They had a goal disallowed for offside before Fotis Ioannidis made it 1-0 after 23 minutes.

The Netherlands offered little going forward and in stoppage time, a bad back pass from Van Bommel led to Giorgos Masouras sliding in a second.

Xavi made a triple change as Gravenberch, Noa Lang and Reijnders came on and they all made a big difference as the Netherlands dominated the second half.

Virgil van Dijk headed one back before Denzel Dumfries had two goals disallowed for offside. Xavi turned to Joshua Zirkzee and debutante Gjivai Zechiel in hope of an equaliser.

The equaliser came in the last minute as Zechiel’s overhead kick dropped into the path of Reijnders who blasted the ball in. Zechiel then came close to a winner but his header was straight at the goalkeeper.

A battling point for the Netherlands, who stay unbeaten under Xavi with a game at home to Serbia to come on Sunday.

The Netherlands came back from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw against Greece in the Nations League. Here is our player ratings for the Netherlands players.

Bart Verbruggen 5.5/10: Wasn’t happy with his defence in the first half. Could have done more for the first goal but did make a good save. Had nothing to do after the break.

Denzel Dumfries 5/10: Struggled in the first half before improving in the second. Had two goals disallowed for offside.

Micky van de Ven 5/10: His pace makes up for the gaps he leaves at times and in the firs half he struggled. Like others he got better in the second but had less to do.

Jurrien Timber 4/10: Looked very much like a player who is not fully fit. Second to everything and gave away fouls in the first half. Was too slow too react for the second goal.

Virgil van Dijk 6/10: Defensively he struggled in the first but his goal got his side back into the game after the break.

Joey Veerman 6.5/10: Always looking to make something happen going forward. Not everything worked but was always available. His corner led to a goal an he almost scored a free kick.

Quinten Timber 4/10: Disastrous display as he gave away foul after foul in the first half. Was rightly hooked at half time.

Guus Til 4/10: Like Timber, he offered nothing in the first half and was rightly taken off. Xavi wanted to give him a chance but he didn’t take it.

Crysencio Summerville 6/10: Was Netherlands only outlet going forward in the first half and is a constant threat on the right hand side.

Ruben van Bommel 4.5/10: Was too static at times and his error led to the second goal. Taken off at the break.

Mexx Meerdink 5/10: Tried but was isolated at times. Had no service in the first half and barely touched the ball in the second.

Noa Lang 7/10: Offered more on the left than Van Bommel as he took the game to the Greek defence. His cross led to the equaliser. Likely to start against Serbia after this display.

Tijjani Reijnders 6.5/10: Came on and scored the equaliser with a good finish. Did a lot more running than Til did and it was much needed energy.

Ryan Gravenberch 6.5/10: Immediately helped the Netherlands midfield gain control back in the second half.

Joshua Zirkzee N/A: Not on the pitch long enough for a review

Gjivai Zechiel N/A: Not on the pitch long enough for a review

FT Greece 2-2 NetherlandsA battling draw after being 2-0 down. Had 2 goals disallowed too! Much better second half but that first half was a disaster

Netherlands edged out Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven to move top of their Nations League group.

Xavi decided to name Teun Koopmeiners in the starting eleven but at centre-back alongside Virgil van Dijk, who was earning his 100th cap. Ryan Gravenberch, Tijjani Reijnders and Noa Lang all came into the eleven.

Netherlands made a strong start and missed two good chances to take the lead within the first two minutes. They then dominated possession but it took until the 31st minute for Oranje to take the lead. Koopmeiners free kick evaded everyone and nestled in the corner.

Oranje were only ahead for four minutes as Mihaijo Cvetkovic was allowed far too much space in the Netherlands box to loop in a header. It could have been worse for the Netherlands before the break but Pavlovic squandered a chance when in on goal.

Xavi brought on Joshua Zirkzee for Mexx Meerdink at the break but the best chances early in the second half were for Serbia. Cvetkovic should have put the visitors ahead.

Xavi turned to the bench again with Gjivai Zechiel, Ruben van Bommel and Jorrel Hato all appearing. Reijnders should have made it 2-1 but when through on goal he scooped the ball over the bar.

Netherlands retook the lead after 72 minutes with Denzel Dumfries crossing for Reijnders to square it to an unmarked Zirkzee, who tapped in. It should have been 3-1 straight away but Reijnders was denied through on goal.

The Netherlands sat back and that allowed Serbia to put on pressure. That pressure increased when Micky van de Ven was forced off and Oranje played the last five minutes with only ten men.

Bart Verbruggen made a big save to deny Nemanja Gudelj and Netherlands managed to hold on for the three points.

Netherlands first four games under Xavi see them win two and draw two. They will finish the Nations League at home to Germany and then away to Greece.

FT Netherlands 2-1 SerbiaIt’s three points but far from convincing in the end. Xavi remains unbeaten in his first four games in charge

#2509. Official: Paul Nebel extends contract with Mainz 05

As officially announced by the Bundesliga club this afternoon, Paul Nebel has extended his contract with 1. FSV Mainz 05.

The midfielder, who joined the club at Bruchweg as a 13-year-old, progressed through all the youth teams at Mainz's academy.

Nebel has worn the 05ers' jersey for over ten years, with the exception of a two-year loan spell at second division side Karlsruher SC.

Still only 24 years of age, Nebel has already made 95 appearances in all competitions for Mainz, providing 15 goals and 18 assists.

“Paul is the prime example of how a player from our own youth academy can develop into a very important player for our Bundesliga team.

“He has shown a lot of passion, patience and a down-to-earth attitude,” explained Mainz sporting director Niko Bungert.

"Paul is an important and reliable pillar for our team and someone who has shown in recent years that he is always there when needed.

"We are happy that we have found a very good solution for our future together with him.”

#2507. Generali Stadium, avvertimento a Inter e Milan: Majorino apre alla revisione, Calabresi vuole ridiscutere

Generali Stadium, avvertimento a Inter e Milan: Majorino apre alla revisione, Calabresi vuole ridiscutere

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Il progetto del nuovo Generali Stadium di Inter e Milan torna al centro del dibattito politico milanese. A riaccendere la discussione sono le dichiarazioni di Pierfrancesco Majorino e Mario Calabresi, entrambi tra gli aspiranti candidati sindaco del centrosinistra in vista delle elezioni comunali del 2027.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Due interventi distinti, ma con un punto in comune: la volontà di rimettere in discussione alcuni aspetti dell'operazione, qualora ci fossero le condizioni per farlo.

Il capogruppo del Pd in Regione Lombardia ha spiegato che entro la primavera del 2027 dovrebbero arrivare alcuni passaggi fondamentali, tra cui la sentenza del Consiglio di Stato e le valutazioni sull'impatto ambientale e sanitario dell'intervento.

A quel punto, secondo Majorino, sarà possibile capire quali margini esistano per intervenire sul progetto.

«Se ci fossero le condizioni per rimettere in discussione il progetto, sarebbe la cosa giusta da fare».

Majorino ha quindi precisato che, qualora l'operazione non fosse più modificabile dal punto di vista formale, diventerebbe fondamentale concentrarsi sulla tutela dei residenti, sulle conseguenze ambientali e sull'utilizzo delle risorse comunali per riqualificare il quartiere San Siro.

Non si tratta, dunque, dell'annuncio di un blocco già deciso, ma di una posizione che lascia aperta la possibilità di modifiche in base agli sviluppi amministrativi e giudiziari.

"Entro la prossima primavera, intanto, saranno chiarite alcune cose, ad esempio ci sarà già stata la sentenza del Consiglio di Stato e avremo visto le valutazioni di impatto ambientale e sulla salute. Se ci fossero le condizioni per rimettere in discussione il progetto, sarebbe la cosa giusta da fare. L’ho già detto mesi fa e non cambio idea. Io in Consiglio comunale mi sarei fatto sentire per cambiare quella delibera. Se, invece, la vicenda di San Siro non sarà modificabile dal punto di vista formale, bisognerà essere attentissimi alle questioni di impatto ambientale per tutelare i residenti del quartiere e sul modo in cui investire le risorse ottenute dal Comune per riqualificare la parte più popolare di San Siro”.

Il giornalista, che ha manifestato la propria disponibilità a partecipare alle primarie del centrosinistra, ha spiegato che, in caso di elezione a sindaco, intende incontrare Inter e Milan per affrontare nuovamente alcuni aspetti dell'operazione.

«Alla luce di quello che sta succedendo alcune cose vanno ridiscusse».

Calabresi ha individuato soprattutto tre questioni: la tutela della salute dei residenti durante i lavori, l'impatto ambientale della costruzione del nuovo impianto e della demolizione del Meazza e la necessità di garantire benefici concreti agli abitanti del quartiere.

Secondo l'aspirante candidato sindaco, le due società dovrebbero assumersi maggiori responsabilità nei confronti del territorio interessato dal progetto.

A suo giudizio, l'intervento dovrebbe essere sostenuto economicamente da Inter e Milan, senza ricadere sulle finanze comunali.

Va però precisato che, secondo il piano illustrato, il costo complessivo dello spostamento è stimato in 68,1 milioni di euro, a carico dei club, con una parte dell'importo coperta attraverso lo scomputo degli oneri di urbanizzazione.

Non sarebbe quindi corretto affermare che, allo stato attuale, l'intera opera sia finanziata direttamente dal Comune.

Il tema dello stadio resta così uno dei principali terreni di confronto politico in vista delle prossime elezioni milanesi.

Per Inter e Milan, che hanno già presentato il progetto del Generali Stadium, le posizioni di Majorino e Calabresi rappresentano un nuovo elemento di attenzione. Le dichiarazioni non modificano automaticamente gli accordi esistenti, ma confermano che il futuro dell'area di San Siro continuerà a essere al centro del dibattito cittadino.

"Il sindaco si è arrabbiato parecchio - ha ammesso Calabresi parlando della reazione di Giuseppe Sala sulle sue critiche sullo stadio -. Io ho detto tre cose, la prima che dobbiamo preoccuparci della salute del quartiere, dell'impatto ambientale della costruzione del nuovo stadio e della demolizione del vecchio. Oggi siamo in quella fase".

Il secondo punto "è che il quartiere non deve pagare un prezzo senza avere nessun tipo di beneficio, di ritorno", ha aggiunto e "lo dico senza che sia lesa maestà, voglio dire la mia". Ad esempio secondo Calabresi lo spostamento del tunnel Patroclo non deve essere pagato dal Comune ma dalle squadre.

"Allora dobbiamo accettare che tutto quello che è stato deciso debba rimanere immobile? - ha spiegato ancora -, le squadre vanno sfidate perché ci sia un impegno sul quartiere superiore". Sul fatto di non abbattere San Siro, "non la penso come La Russa perché dico cose che lui non ha detto - ha rivendicato infine -. Sullo stadio dobbiamo essere laici".

#2506. « Cela aurait pu être ma fille » : Thierry Henry exprime sa profonde colère et son indignation sur le plateau de CBS

Sur le plateau de CBS Sports lors de la soirée de Ligue des champions ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, Thierry Henry a tenu à prendre la parole pour évoquer l'attentat raciste survenu dans les Yvelines. Un moment de grande émotion pour l'ancien attaquant des Bleus, profondément touché par ce drame.

Mardi soir, alors que les débats sportifs battaient leur plein autour des affiches européennes, Thierry Henry a choisi d'interrompre l'analyse pour aborder l'attentat raciste perpétré le 23 octobre 2026 à Trappes et La Verrière. Une prise de parole rare et solennelle en plein direct. L'ancien international français a livré un message sincère, visiblement ému par les événements survenus en région parisienne.

Son intervention a immédiatement été saluée sur le plateau de l'émission américaine. Ainsi, ses collègues consultants Jamie Carragher et Micah Richards ont salué ses propos par des applaudissements appuyés, marquant leur respect pour son engagement et sa dignité face à cette tragédie.

Au-delà de la compassion, Thierry Henry a insisté sur son histoire personnelle pour expliquer à quel point ce drame le touchait de près. Père de famille français, noir et originaire de la région parisienne, l'ex-buteur a partagé son sentiment de révolte et d'inquiétude pour les siens. « Je suis noir, je suis français, je suis père de famille. Cela aurait pu être mon frère, cela aurait pu être ma fille. Alors, cela doit cesser », a-t-il déclaré avec gravité face aux caméras.

L'ancien champion a également exprimé son incompréhension face aux remises en question de l'appartenance nationale. « À un moment donné, ça suffit. On se promène dans la rue et on se fait tuer, tout simplement. Est-ce que nous devons toujours prouver que nous sommes français ? Nous sommes français et cela ne changera jamais, quoi qu’il arrive », a poursuivi Thierry Henry sur le plateau de CBS Sports.

En effet, l'attaque survenue le 23 octobre 2026 à Trappes et La Verrière a fait un mort et sept blessés, dont une jeune fille de 12 ans. L'assaillant présumé, un homme de 39 ans, a été mis en examen et placé en détention provisoire après avoir reconnu avoir ciblé délibérément des personnes musulmanes, africaines ou nord-africaines. Un choc immense pour les familles.

Thierry Henry a tenu à honorer la mémoire de Pengo Bossio Wangi, combattant de MMA de 26 ans tué lors de cet attentat : « Je souhaite simplement rendre hommage et témoigner mon respect aux familles des victimes, et évidemment à la famille de Pengo, qui a perdu la vie simplement parce qu’il était noir. Je voulais simplement apporter un peu de soutien à toutes les personnes qui ont souffert de cet événement. Comme je l’ai dit, je vais me répéter : ça suffit ».

Giovanni van Bronckhorst, allenatore del Feyenoord, ha analizzato la sconfitta contro l'Inter in conferenza stampa in vista della sfida di campionato contro l'Heerenveen.

"Ci siamo allenati mercoledì e ieri abbiamo avuto un giorno di riposo. Abbiamo rivisto l'Inter e l'Heerenveen, come facciamo sempre. L’ex arbitro Marco Gabriele analizza a livello regolamentare la rete di Andrea Pinamonti contro il Cagliari

L’ex arbitro Marco Gabriele è intervenuto ai microfoni di Radio Radio per esaminare il discusso gol di Andrea Pinamonti, arrivato sul finale di Lazio-Cagliari. L'episodio continua a far discutere poiché la rete del 2-1 è nata mentre Deiola era rimasto a terra dopo una pallonata, con il gioco che è proseguito regolarmente fino alla conclusione vincente dell'attaccante.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

A mio avviso Colombo ha gestito correttamente la situazione e la rete è regolare. Dopo la conclusione di Dele-Bashiru, il pallone è rimasto per alcuni secondi a disposizione dei giocatori del Cagliari, prima che l’azione proseguisse. Questo è un elemento importante nella valutazione dell’episodio.

L’arbitro non è obbligato a interrompere automaticamente il gioco ogni volta che un calciatore viene colpito dal pallone. Lo deve fare quando ritiene che ci sia un infortunio grave. Per questo, secondo la mia valutazione, Colombo ha fatto bene a lasciar proseguire l’azione.

#2503. « Une décision inattendue, que l’OL regrette profondément » : Le communiqué amer de l'Olympique Lyonnais officialisant le départ de Paulo Fonseca

Ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, l'Olympique Lyonnais a officialisé le départ de Paulo Fonseca de ses fonctions d'entraîneur de l'équipe professionnelle vers le Sporting Portugal. Dans un communiqué au ton particulièrement piquant, la direction rhodanienne a fustigé le timing de cette décision inattendue et l'engagement du technicien.

La nouvelle a surpris tout le monde à Lyon. Alors que son contrat avec l'OL courait initialement jusqu'au 30 juin 2027, Paulo Fonseca a lui-même informé ses dirigeants de sa volonté de partir. Le technicien de 53 ans a en effet été approché ces derniers jours par le Sporting Portugal, un club auquel il est particulièrement attaché. Pour racheter son contrat, la formation portugaise versera d'ailleurs une indemnité de 5 millions d'euros à l'OL. Toutefois, cette indemnité ne console pas les décideurs lyonnais.

Arrivé le 31 janvier 2025, Paulo Fonseca a dirigé son 83e et dernier match dimanche 1er novembre 2026 lors de la victoire contre Angers (2-0) au Groupama Stadium. Il quitte Lyon en laissant le club à la 3e place de Ligue 1 avec 17 points, pour un bilan de 5 victoires, 2 nuls et 2 défaites. Une dynamique sportive positive qui rend la séparation d'autant plus amère pour l'OL.

Au-delà de la surprise créée par cette demande, ce sont surtout les termes choisis par l'OL dans son communiqué qui détonnent. Loin des formules polies d'usage, l'état-major lyonnais a pointé du doigt l'attitude de son entraîneur. La direction a ainsi estimé qu'il « n'était pas dans l'intérêt du club de poursuivre une collaboration qui ne pouvait plus garantir le niveau d'engagement total indispensable à la réussite du projet ». Un reproche cinglant adressé au Portugais.

En effet, le club rhodanien a insisté sur le fait que dans « une période aussi déterminante de la saison », l'ensemble des forces devait être « entièrement mobilisé et concentré sur les objectifs ». Face à un entraîneur désireux d'ailleurs, l'OL a préféré trancher immédiatement dans le vif. La direction s'active désormais pour identifier un successeur au profil capable de s'inscrire dans la continuité du projet sportif et des principes développés ces derniers mois.

Dans l'immédiat, l'Olympique Lyonnais a dû réagir rapidement pour gérer le quotidien. C'est Jorge Maciel qui a été désigné pour assurer l'intérim à la tête de l'équipe professionnelle jusqu'à la prochaine trêve internationale de novembre 2026. Le technicien va devoir prendre le relais sans temps d'adaptation avant deux déplacements importants.

Jorge Maciel dirigera ainsi les Gones face à la Real Sociedad ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026 à 18h45 au stade d'Anoeta, dans le cadre de la Ligue Europa. Dans la foulée, le technicien conduira également le groupe lyonnais lors du déplacement en Ligue 1 à Brest, prévu le dimanche 8 novembre 2026 à 17h15.

#2502. « La vie ne se résume pas à gagner des courses cyclistes » : les confidences touchantes de Pauline Ferrand-Prévot après son année 2026 difficile

Pauline Ferrand-Prévot est sortie de plusieurs mois de silence pour évoquer ouvertement son état d'esprit et sa santé mentale. La leader de la formation Visma | Lease a Bike a pris la parole sur ses réseaux sociaux pour annoncer le terme d'une longue pause salutaire après son abandon lors du Tour de France Femmes.

Après une saison 2025 très réussie marquée par ses sacres sur Paris-Roubaix et la Grande Boucle, la championne rémoise de 34 ans a traversé un exercice 2026 bien plus contrasté, sans victoires majeures malgré des podiums sur le Tour des Flandres et Paris-Roubaix. En difficulté pour rivaliser avec les meilleures sur La Vuelta puis contrainte à l'abandon avant le départ de la 8e étape du Tour de France Femmes cet été selon les bilans de course, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot n'avait plus épinglé le moindre dossard en compétition depuis lors.

Éprouvée par cette spirale négative, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot a décidé de s'éloigner des pelotons pour faire redescendre une immense pression sportive. Sur son compte Instagram, la représentante de Visma | Lease a Bike a expliqué combien la quête absolue du résultat avait fini par étouffer son quotidien : « J’étais tellement focalisée sur l’idée de gagner à nouveau le Tour que j’en avais perdu la joie du quotidien. Tout tournait autour de la performance, de l’exigence constante de faire toujours plus pour être la meilleure. »

Face à une saison blanche de grands trophées en dépit d'une rigueur absolue, la championne a reconnu avoir été totalement surprise par cet échec sportif : « Par le passé, j’avais déjà traversé des périodes difficiles, où je me sentais triste et perdue. Mais je n’avais jamais vécu une situation où, malgré tous mes efforts et une préparation irréprochable, je me retrouvais finalement avec rien. C’est sans doute ce qui explique pourquoi, ces derniers mois, je n’arrivais tout simplement pas à comprendre ce qui m’arrivait. » Pour surmonter cette surcharge mentale, elle s'est donc accordé une vraie coupure en famille, loin des sacrifices habituels : « Depuis le Tour, j’ai parfois repris mon vélo, tout en m’accordant des plaisirs que je m’étais interdits durant toute la saison. J’ai passé du temps avec ma famille, profité des choses simples et savouré des moments précieux, loin du vélo. »

Au-delà de la sphère sportive, les récentes événements de sa vie personnelle ont profondément redéfini l'ordre de ses priorités. Le mercredi 7 octobre 2026, son compagnon Dylan van Baarle, qui court sous les couleurs de la formation Soudal Quick-Step, a été victime d'un accident de la circulation à l'entraînement ayant nécessité une intervention chirurgicale au poignet. Cet événement traumatisant a représenté un déclic majeur pour relativiser l'importance du sport de haut niveau dans son existence.

« Cet incident m’a fait prendre conscience que la vie ne se résume pas à gagner des courses cyclistes. Voir l’être que j’aime le plus au monde traverser une épreuve aussi douloureuse m’a permis de remettre les choses en perspective. Pour une fois, j’étais 'heureuse' de pouvoir être à ses côtés et de faire tout mon possible pour le soutenir. D’habitude, c’est toujours lui qui prend soin de moi », a détaillé la coureuse tricolore. Ainsi, le couple s'est marié fin octobre 2026 aux Pays-Bas au cours d'une cérémonie intime célébrée par la mère de Dylan van Baarle. « Je me souviens avoir ressenti beaucoup de joie en remportant les Jeux olympiques, le Tour ou Paris-Roubaix, mais épouser Dylan, entourée des personnes les plus importantes de ma vie, a procuré un bonheur et un épanouissement d’une tout autre dimension », a-t-elle confié sur le réseau social. Une étape fondamentale dans sa reconstruction.

Désormais apaisée, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot ne songe absolument pas à prendre sa retraite, elle dont le contrat avec la formation Visma | Lease a Bike court jusqu'à la fin de l'année 2028 selon des informations de presse. Toutefois, la coureuse ne compte brûler aucune étape avant d'envisager son grand retour à la compétition, constatant en toute lucidité la perte de sa condition physique : « Et voilà, c’est la fin d’une très longue intersaison, dont j’avais grand besoin. »

« Cette longue intersaison m’était vraiment nécessaire. Le chemin sera long pour retrouver un niveau correct, car je ne suis plus du tout en forme. Mais, pour l’instant, l’essentiel est de retrouver le plaisir d’être sur un vélo », a enchaîné la Rémoise. D'ailleurs, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot a d'ores et déjà fixé l'échéance de sa reprise de l'entraînement dès le mois de janvier afin de préparer la saison 2027. Un travail de longue haleine qu'elle aborde avec sérénité et une réelle envie : « Je suis sûre que je reviendrai plus forte. » Le premier coup de pédale est programmé pour janvier.

#2501. Une première pour un Français depuis 10 ans : Arthur Fils se qualifie pour les Finales ATP de Turin !

Ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, Arthur Fils a validé mathématiquement sa qualification pour les Finales ATP de Turin, organisées du 15 au 22 novembre prochain. Le Français profite de l'exploit d'un autre Français, Quentin Halys, qui a éliminé Frances Tiafoe au Rolex Paris Masters.

Le dénouement s'est joué sur le court central de la Plénitude Arena à Nanterre. Opposé à l'Américain Frances Tiafoe, tête de série numéro 7 et 8e à la Race, Quentin Halys a signé une performance remarquable au deuxième tour du Rolex Paris Masters. Le 46e joueur mondial s'est imposé au terme d'un duel de 1 heure et 57 minutes (6-1, 3-6, 7-6 [9]). Frances Tiafoe servait pourtant pour le match à 5-4 dans la troisième manche, avant que Halys n'efface quatre balles de match dans le jeu décisif.

Un exploit retentissant. En se hissant en huitièmes de finale, Quentin Halys a précipité la fin des espoirs de l'Américain. En effet, ce revers de Frances Tiafoe valide définitivement la présence d'Arthur Fils à Turin parmi les huit meilleurs joueurs de la planète.

Cette qualification met fin à une longue attente pour le clan tricolore. Arthur Fils devient ainsi le premier joueur français à rallier les ATP Finals depuis Gaël Monfils en 2016. Une première depuis dix ans. À Turin, du 15 au 22 novembre 2026, il deviendra d'ailleurs le 10e joueur de l'histoire du tennis français à disputer ce prestigieux tournoi des maîtres de fin de saison.

La route menant Arthur Fils aux Finales ATP s'est révélée particulièrement atypique. En effet, le Français a manqué l'Open d'Australie et Roland-Garros en 2026 en raison de blessures, tout en restant discret à Wimbledon comme à l'US Open. Ainsi, il devient le premier joueur qualifié pour le Masters avec moins de deux matches gagnés en Grand Chelem sur une saison depuis Brad Gilbert en 1989.

Tête de série numéro 6, Arthur Fils dispute son deuxième tour du Rolex Paris Masters ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 face à Tomas Machac, sur le court central, pas avant 20h30.

#2499. « J’ai accepté cette proposition avec beaucoup d’enthousiasme » : Rafael Nadal prend du galon au Real Madrid !

Le conseil d'administration du Real Madrid a officialisé ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 la proposition d'intégrer Rafael Nadal au sein de son Conseil d’administration. Une arrivée majeure pour le club de la capitale et son président Florentino Pérez, qui doit désormais être soumise au vote des socios.

Réuni ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, le conseil d'administration du Real Madrid a convenu de soumettre à l'assemblée générale des socios la ratification de la nomination de Rafael Nadal Parera comme nouveau membre de son Conseil d’administration. Cette proposition intervient en application de l'article 46 des statuts sociaux du club madrilène. Âgé de 40 ans et retraité des courts depuis 2024, le champion espagnol aux 22 tournois du Grand Chelem, dont un record de 14 victoires à Roland-Garros, franchit ainsi une étape institutionnelle majeure. Une figure emblématique du sport mondial au service du club de son cœur.

D'ailleurs, l'ancienne star du tennis n'arrive pas en terre inconnue dans la capitale espagnole, puisqu'il est socio d'honneur du Real Madrid et porte le numéro de socio 67 778. Dans un communiqué officiel publié ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, l'institution madrilène a salué cette future arrivée : « Le Conseil d’administration du Real Madrid CF, réuni ce mercredi 4 novembre, a décidé de soumettre à l’Assemblée générale des membres délégués la ratification de la nomination de Rafael Nadal Parera, membre numéro 67 778 de notre club, en tant que nouveau membre du Conseil d’administration. Rafael Nadal, membre honoraire du Real Madrid, est l’une des plus grandes légendes de l’histoire du sport et l’un des athlètes espagnols les plus admirés et reconnus au monde. Pour le Real Madrid et pour tous les supporters madrilènes, c’est une grande fierté qu’une figure de son envergure sportive et humaine, une référence du sport espagnol et mondial, rejoigne notre conseil d’administration et contribue, depuis cette position à responsabilité, au présent et à l’avenir de notre club ».

Dans la foulée de cette annonce, Rafael Nadal a réagi publiquement sur ses réseaux sociaux pour partager son sentiment, en publiant une photo de lui enfant portant le maillot du Real Madrid et en remerciant le dirigeant merengue. « Je tiens à remercier le président Florentino Pérez et le conseil d’administration de m’avoir proposé de rejoindre le conseil d’administration du Real Madrid. J’ai accepté cette proposition avec beaucoup d’enthousiasme, l’envie d’apprendre et de m’investir autant que possible », a confié l'Espagnol.

Cet engagement clarifie la place de l'Espagnol au sein de la Maison Blanche. Plus tôt au cours de l'année 2026, Rafael Nadal avait déjà démenti sur ses réseaux sociaux les rumeurs l'associant à une éventuelle candidature à la présidence du club. Pas question de viser le sommet de l'organigramme pour l'instant. Il s'agit uniquement d'un rôle d'administrateur, où il entend apporter sa contribution au présent et au futur du Real Madrid.

Toutefois, l'intégration de la légende espagnole n'est pas encore définitivement actée. La ratification de sa nomination sera formellement soumise au vote des socios délégués lors d'une assemblée générale extraordinaire convoquée le samedi 21 novembre 2026. Cette réunion se tiendra au pavillon de basket de la Ciudad Real Madrid, immédiatement après l'assemblée générale ordinaire, avec pour unique point à l'ordre du jour la validation de l'entrée de Rafael Nadal.

Sur le plan sportif, le Real Madrid dispute ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 à 18h45 un match contre l'AEK Athènes à l'Allwyn Arena pour la 4e journée de Ligue des champions. Les Madrilènes enchaîneront ensuite avec un déplacement en Liga contre le Valence CF à Mestalla, programmé le samedi 7 novembre 2026 à 21h00.
